cases.description: Strict policy: a child of a timed-out script that ignores TERM is killed with the whole process group before the run returns.
cases.name: post.sh

list/post.sh.body:
( trap '' TERM; exec 3<>"$PFB_TEST_ALIVE"; echo up > "$PFB_TEST_CHILD"; read -r _ < "$PFB_TEST_BLOCK" ) &
echo $! > "$PFB_TEST_PID"
read -r _ < "$PFB_TEST_CHILD"
echo started
pfb_block

[ hdr ] post-script 'post.sh' TIMED OUT (killed); discarding its output

cases.departure: GNU timeout(1) exits once its direct child is gone, leaving a child that ignored TERM running; FreeBSD's reaper timeout(1) kills it after the grace, as Core does when the leader exits (the strict policy).

cases.description: A script that backgrounds a process holding its stdout open and exits: the run returns at the script's exit without waiting for the process, which the strict policy kills with the group.
cases.name: post.sh

list/post.sh.body:
( exec 3<>"$PFB_TEST_ALIVE"; echo up > "$PFB_TEST_CHILD"; read -r _ < "$PFB_TEST_BLOCK" ) &
echo $! > "$PFB_TEST_PID"
read -r _ < "$PFB_TEST_CHILD"
echo leader done

cases.departure: GNU timeout(1) returns at the script's exit and leaves the process running; FreeBSD's reaper timeout(1) waits for it until the 300-second limit and then reports a timeout. Core returns at the script's exit and kills the process group (the strict policy).
